newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Energy Dept defends fossil energy research.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Energy Dept defends fossil energy research.

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department said it would be unwise to eliminate its fossil energy research and development programs, as proposed Tuesday by an alliance of left and right-wing groups, and backed by House Budget Committee Chairman John Kasich of Ohio.

"We have to be careful when we begin to cut back on the advanced research that is critical to helping the industry to lower its costs and develop more of our domestic resources," said Kyle Simpson, associate deputy secretary of energy.

The programs, whose costs are often shared with the industry and university laboratories, help spread new oil and natural gas production and processing technologies quickly. That "helps keep our energy costs lower," he told Reuters.

Targeting "corporate welfare," the alliance -- including the conservative Americans for Tax Reform and the environmental group Friends of the Earth -- said the government could save $1.37 billion in one year by eliminating research on applied fossil energy technologies.

But Simpson said that would put U.S. companies at disadvantage. "In an increasingly competitive energy environment, where governments around the world are taking a very active role, often much more than us, we have a responsibility to help keep our nation's energy advantage," he said.
